translationRepairs: Wang Gong of Shaanzhou fought his brother Ke for Hezhong; he sent Sizhao to aid Ke, beat Gong at Yishi, and took three of his generals.
Wang Gong of Shaanzhou contended with his elder brother Ke for control of Hezhong. Taizu sent Sizhao to aid Ke; Sizhao defeated Gong at Yishi and captured three of his generals.
Taizu is the omitted subject of 遣, while Sizhao remains the subject of 敗 and 獲. The proposal correctly removes Gong as sender but wrongly makes Ke the victor.
Wang Gong of Shaan Prefecture contended with his elder brother Ke for rule in Hezhong; he sent Sizhao to aid Ke and defeated Gong at Yishi, capturing three of his generals.
Wang Gong of Shaan Prefecture contended with his elder brother Ke for rule in Hezhong; Taizu sent Sizhao to aid Ke, and Sizhao defeated Gong at Yishi, capturing three of his generals.
Taizu is the omitted subject of 遣, while Sizhao remains the subject of 敗 and 獲. The proposal correctly removes Gong as sender but wrongly makes Ke the victor.
Hearing Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled straight into the ambush and was crushed.
Hearing Liang Taizu had come himself, Sizhao abandoned the city and fled straight into the ambush and was crushed.
Chinese 梁太祖 is Liang Taizu; dropping Liang conflates him with Jin Taizu in the same chapter.
At Willow Hu Jin lost; Zhou Dewei fell.
At Huliu, Jin lost; Zhou Dewei fell.
胡柳 is the place Huliu (Huliu Slope), not a calque 'Willow Hu'; the current rendering obscures the battle name.
Taizu panicked and planned escape to Yunzhou; Cunxin urged flight to the Khitan; Sizhao and Consort Liu protested until he stayed.
Taizu panicked and planned escape to Yunzhou; Cunxin and others urged flight to the Khitan; Sizhao protested that it was impossible, and Consort Liu said the same, so he stopped.
Chinese 李存信等 includes companions, and 嗣昭力爭 / 劉太妃亦言之 are separate speeches, not a fused joint protest.

太尉 is Grand Commandant (or Defender-in-chief), not Grand Preceptor (太師/太傅).
